market.domesticSlice: India-specific figures; largely a domestic-consumption category

structureFacts: India's electric fan market is large and growing quickly (~11% CAGR), but the organized/branded segment is only an estimated ~20% of it — the majority of the market remains unorganized, which is both a competitive threat (price-driven, low-differentiation competition) and a headroom opportunity (formalization/branding upside) for any established manufacturer.

The branded/organized segment is dominated by a small number of large, listed, national names (Crompton Greaves, Havells, Orient Electric, Usha International, Bajaj Electricals, Khaitan Electricals, Surya Roshni, Almonard, Luminous) plus Polycab, which itself both makes fans and sources components — creating a real OEM/component-supply layer beneath the branded majors that a smaller manufacturer can occupy without competing head-on for retail shelf space.

The Indian Fan Manufacturers Association (IFMA) is a real, active industry trade body that runs recognized award competitions (e.g. the AM Competition) — a credible, checkable venue for industry standing distinct from a government registry.

adoptionStructure.note: A mix of B2C retail demand (branded consumer fans) and B2B/OEM component supply (parts and sub-assemblies sold into larger brands' supply chains) — the second channel is less visible publicly but can be a substantial, stable revenue base for a specialized manufacturer.

drivers: Reliability and consistency of component supply for OEM/B2B relationships — a supplier that has run continuously for 67 years under stable family ownership is a lower-risk long-term vendor.
Price and quality within the largely price-driven unorganized-adjacent segment.
Certification/compliance credentials (ISO, industry-body recognition) as a baseline trust signal for institutional/B2B buyers, distinct from consumer brand appeal.
customerValue.strongestPredictor: Demonstrated manufacturing consistency and technical capability over a long operating history — in a component-supply relationship, a buyer cares more about a vendor's ability to keep delivering to spec for years than about brand marketing.
